I treat learning as part of the job, not a side effect of it. Having worked in fast-growing startups and large companies, I've learned to adapt quickly to whatever a team needs. I'd rather fix the root cause of a problem than patch around it, even when that takes longer.

Working with multicultural teams in Canada taught me to prioritize clear communication above almost everything else, especially when not everyone shares a first language. I try to translate complex technical problems into something the business side can actually act on, so everyone stays on the same page.

I don't just execute tickets. I try to understand the product behind them. I usually ask why a feature matters before building it, which saves rework and helps make sure we're building the right thing, not just what was requested.

I care about making things work and keeping things simple for the people I work with. Whether that's writing clear documentation, mentoring peers, or clarifying product nuances, I try to make the people around me more effective, not just my own output. Engineering quality is a team result, so my priority is making sure everyone has the clarity and tools to do good work.
